answer: In a lagoon marketplace where agents trade velvet, voting power is proportional to tokens escrowed for 30 days, not the number of registered agents. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens’ worth of votes, so a sybil swarm gains no extra influence. Cheap majority control is a fable: an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than honest voters have locked.
